verdict.rationale: FireHydrant documents a public REST API with token-based API keys and bot tokens, and states the API can do "anything you can do on the FireHydrant UI." An OpenAPI 3.0.1 document targeting api.firehydrant.io is published in the official MCP repo. The probe's 404s on docs-domain OpenAPI paths only show the spec is not hosted at those paths; they do not contradict the API's existence. missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of driving the product end-to-end via the API, a spec published at the docs domain's standard paths.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can drive the product through a documented public API

citations.quote: You can use the FireHydrant API to configure integrations, define incidents, and set up webhooks--anything you can do on the FireHydrant UI.
FireHydrant allows you to access the API with an API key using token-based authentication.
FireHydrant supports bot tokens to act on behalf of a computer instead of a user's account.
The official freshworks-oss/firehydrant-mcp repository publishes a FireHydrant OpenAPI document (.speakeasy/openapi.output.yaml)
